title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model error. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems is alleged to have queried them for a purpose unrelated to policing, turning licence plate readers and a criminal justice database into a private tracking tool. The failure sits at the point of use, in the gap between what an authorised account can do and what it is supposed to be used for.

The controls that would catch this are access logging and audit, not model accuracy. The systems recorded the queries, and the alleged conduct surfaced through an investigation rather than through the software refusing the request. Detecting it earlier would have required someone reviewing query logs against case justification, or a flag on searches tied to no active investigation.

The indictment charges are allegations and the case has not been tried, so guilt is not established. The reporting also does not establish how the queries were discovered or what internal review, if any, preceded the referral to the GBI.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff's deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, has been released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violating his oath, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege that between April and May 2024, Rozar misused the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons, including tracking and surveilling a woman without her consent. He was terminated when the investigation began, and former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested the GBI investigate in 2024.

The woman at the center of the allegations spoke anonymously to WALB, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to come forward and that she waited two years for the investigation to finish. Rozar was taken into custody on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled to appear for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
